hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.1-0.15.
Response has thermal lag with time constant tens to low hundreds of seconds, not instantaneous and no large pure delay.
No large dead zone: small u >0.1 produces measurable heating; dead zone <0.1 if any.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with no strong saturation below the soft limit.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior around 0.3-0.7, not at 0 or 1.
Sensor noise is small with short-term fluctuations <0.01, so trends are interpretable.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Direction and magnitude of gain and lag/time-constant, which determines all subsequent safe step sizes and hold times.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case y = 0.1525 + 0.006*0.5*200 = 0.7525, which stays below soft limit 0.85 with ~0.10 margin.
proposal.expected_observation: If heating hypothesis is right, y rises monotonically from ~0.15 with short lag then decreasing slope toward ~0.3-0.5, end slope still positive, noise under ~0.01.
proposal.readiness_justification: Zero experiments completed, below minimum of 3; gain, lag, decay rate, linearity, steady-state hold input and noise are all unresolved and needed for controller design.
proposal.operator_note: First probe: half power for 200 s to measure heating direction, rate and lag.

proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is current y 0.528 + 0.006*0.0*480 = 0.528, well below soft limit 0.85, since u=0 cannot drive heating even with no decay or lag.

proposal.readiness_justification: Only E1 completed so readiness requires at least 3 experiments; gain sign and one steady point u=0.5->~0.52 are resolved, but u=0 decay rate and ambient, time constant, linearity/second level, exact hold input for 0.5, dead-zone, and noise level remain unresolved and are needed for safe controller design.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping heater to zero for a long soak to measure natural cooldown, ambient level, and cooling lag.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Near-target steady-state gain and exact hold power for y=0.5 given apparent concave nonlinearity between 0.25->0.41 and 0.5->0.52, which sets controller feedforward and gain.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound 0.4152+0.006*0.4*170=0.823 stays below soft limit 0.85, and passive heat loss and short 170s duration keep true level far from hard cutoff 0.9.

proposal.operator_note: Stepping up slightly to 0.4 for a short hold to measure near-target gain without approaching limits.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.12-0.16.
Response has thermal lag with time constant ~80-180s plus small pure delay ~10-25s, not instantaneous.
No large dead zone: u=0.25 produces clear heating from ambient; any dead zone <0.1.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with no saturation below soft limit.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior ~0.32-0.40: u=0.25 holds ~0.41 below target, u=0.4 holds ~0.53 above target, u=0.5 holds ~0.52 above target.
Short-term sensor fluctuations/noise are ~0.02-0.04, larger than 0.01 and comparable to band half-width 0.025, requiring filtering/deadband.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Local steady-state gain near target and exact hold power for y=0.5 under apparent saturation (0.25->0.41 vs 0.4->0.53 vs 0.5->0.52), which sets controller feedforward and whether integral must handle concave nonlinearity.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound using current y=0.5328 is 0.5328+0.006*0.32*160=0.8400 below soft limit 0.85, so even with no decay or lag the soft limit cannot be reached and hard cutoff 0.9 is not approached.
proposal.expected_observation: If saturating/concave model with tau ~100-150s is right, y decays from ~0.533 toward ~0.46-0.48, reaching ~0.49-0.50 after 160s with small negative end slope ~-0.0002 and noise +/-0.02; if linear model were right, drop would be larger toward ~0.37.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, decay to ambient, and lag range are resolved well enough for stable tuning, but exact hold power for y=0.5 remains bracketed only between 0.25 and 0.4 with evidence of saturation, and downward local gain near target has not been observed; one small step-down from current 0.53 is needed to pin feedforward and confirm downward controllability before designing controller.
proposal.operator_note: Stepping power down slightly to 0.32 to find the exact setting that holds target temperature.

hypotheses.statement: Increasing u increases y: steady-state gain and initial slope are positive.
At u=0 y decays on its own toward a low ambient near 0.12-0.16.
Response has thermal lag with time constant ~150-200s plus small pure delay ~10-25s, not instantaneous.
No large dead zone: u=0.25 produces clear heating from ambient; any dead zone <0.1.
Steady-state response is approximately linear in u with K~1.0; apparent saturation is truncation because short holds are only ~1 tau.
Steady-state u needed to hold y=0.5 is interior ~0.32-0.38 centered ~0.34.
Short-term sensor fluctuations/noise are ~0.02-0.04, comparable to band half-width 0.025, requiring filtering/deadband.
Change is weaker actuator: same u gives ~30-50% smaller steady rise, but u=0 cooling rate, ambient, delay and sensor unchanged; u~0.38 now holds only ~0.36-0.37.
Change is faster outflow: fall at u=0 is faster and steady level for same u is lower, ambient may be lower.
Change is slower dynamics: pure delay and/or tau noticeably increased, so response to command change starts later and approaches slower.
Change is sensor offset downward ~0.10-0.14 with true thermal dynamics unchanged.
Change is sensor noise/quantization change: increased dropouts, repeats/flat readings, different variance with dynamics unchanged.

proposal.uncertainty_targeted: Delay from last command change plus u=0 fall rate and ambient, which discriminates faster outflow (faster/lower fall) vs longer delay (later start of fall) vs weaker gain or sensor offset (same fall shape as E2) and reveals sensor noise.
proposal.safety_argument: Worst-case bound is 0.3567 + 0.006*0*480 = 0.3567, well below soft limit 0.85; margin ~0.49 covers in-transit ~0.39 command even with 60s delay (~0.14 rise).
proposal.expected_observation: If weaker-gain hypothesis is right, y holds near 0.35-0.37 for ~20-30s (delay, still responding to prior ~0.39 in transit, possibly tiny rise), then falls monotonically toward ~0.12-0.16, reaching ~0.20 within ~200s and near-flat by ~350-400s with end slope ~0 and noise +/-0.02, matching E2 shape.
proposal.readiness_justification: Direction, ambient and noise are known from discovery, but gain vs loss vs delay vs sensor offset are confounded in closed-loop after-change trace; a clean u=0 delay/cooling measurement is needed before a gain test, so not ready to generate.
proposal.operator_note: Draining at zero power to measure delay and cooling rate to separate gain, loss, delay and sensor effects.
